1. Core Clinical Tension: An oncologic patient with a history of resected lung adenocarcinoma following adjuvant chemotherapy presenting with a new enlarging hypermetabolic subpleural nodule (SUVmax 6.1) on PET-CT, creating an intense diagnostic dilemma between recurrent malignant disease and a granulomatous infectious process in the setting of normal serum tumor markers.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation ends after advanced non-invasive imaging (chest CT, normal serum tumor markers, and PET-CT demonstrating intense FDG avidity) has established high suspicion for recurrent neoplasm, immediately prior to the confirmatory video-assisted thoracoscopic lung biopsy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Recurrent/metastatic bronchogenic adenocarcinoma is strongly suggested by FDG hypermetabolism (SUVmax 6.1) but contradicted by stable serum tumor markers and definitively excluded by histopathologic biopsy demonstrating Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
case_prompt:
A 67-year-old male was evaluated in the surgical outpatient department for follow-up of previously resected right lung adenocarcinoma with visceral pleural invasion, for which he had undergone video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy and four cycles of adjuvant cisplatin and gemcitabine chemotherapy, remaining disease-free for nearly three years.

Surveillance chest computed tomography (CT) performed at 32 months postoperatively revealed the appearance of multiple patchy shadows in the right lung. Over the subsequent 9 months of follow-up, serial chest radiographs showed no evident changes, and serum tumor marker tests remained within normal limits.

A repeat chest CT scan obtained after the 9-month observation period revealed a newly visible 0.5 × 0.5 cm subpleural nodule along with slight enlargement of the patchy shadow in the right lung. Subsequent 18F-FDG PET-CT imaging demonstrated intense metabolic activity within the subpleural nodule with a maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of 6.1, strongly suggestive of recurrent malignant disease.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary concern given the patient's oncologic history and intense FDG avidity (SUVmax 6.1) of the enlarging subpleural nodule on PET-CT; ruled out when invasive tissue biopsy demonstrated infectious granulomatous pathology rather than tumor recurrence, consistent with stable serum tumor markers.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: PET-CT scans revealed that the FDG uptake of the nodule had a SUVmax of 6.1. A that indicated malignant disease.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered during the 9-month period of observation when radiographs and serum tumor markers showed no progression; ruled out by subsequent CT demonstrating enlargement of the patchy opacities, emergence of the subpleural nodule, and marked hypermetabolism.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient did not present any evident changes in the chest radiographs and serum tumor marker tests during the subsequent nine-month follow-up period.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic pivot was achieved via video-assisted thoracoscopic biopsy of the hypermetabolic nodule, which disproved malignancy and confirmed active tuberculosis infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A video-assisted thoracoscopic biopsy indicated that the patient suffered from tuberculosis (Fig. 3).
